title: Where is the bank?
title_target: Πού είναι η τράπεζα; — Poo ee-neh ee trah-peh-zah;
goal: Ask for and give directions — and master the one word fusion that most clearly shows whether your Greek sounds native or translated: σε + the article.
bekal: fuse σε with the article into στον, στη, στο
use one word for both "at/in" and "to"
describe position with δίπλα, κοντά, πίσω, απέναντι
name the public places in a city

dialogs.title: ΔΙΑΛΟΓΟΣ — Asking on the street
dialogs.intro: Ana gets lost around Monastiraki and asks an older man sitting at a café. Count how many times **στο** and its relatives appear — seven times in eleven lines.

lines.speaker: Άννα:
lines.id: Excuse me, where is the bank?

lines.speaker: Κύριος:
lines.id: The bank? It's on the square, next to the pharmacy.
lines.literal: the — bank? it-is — in-the — square, next — to-the — pharmacy.

lines.speaker: Κύριος:
lines.id: No, five minutes on foot. Just go straight ahead.
lines.literal: no, five — minutes — with — the — feet. go — straight.

lines.speaker: Κύριος:
lines.id: Then right, at the corner. The bank is opposite the supermarket.
lines.literal: after — right, at-the — corner. the — bank — it-is — opposite — from — the — supermarket.

lines.id: And the metro? Where's the station?
lines.literal: and — the — metro? where — it-is — the — station?

lines.speaker: Κύριος:

lines.literal: the — station — it-is — behind — from — the — church, between — to-the (pl.) — shops.

lines.id: I go to the square, then to the station. OK!

lines.id: Exactly. Good luck with your Greek!

notes: ⚠️ **σε never stands before the article — the two always fuse.** There's no *σε το σπίτι*, only **στο σπίτι**. No *σε την Αθήνα*, only **στην Αθήνα**. This is beginners' mistake number one, and people hear it at once. Learn the six forms as one chunk.

**σε means "at / in" AND "to" at the same time.** *Είμαι **στην** Αθήνα* = I'm in Athens. *Πάω **στην** Αθήνα* = I'm going to Athens. The verb decides, not the preposition. ⚠️ For English speakers used to choosing between *in*, *at*, and *to*, this is actually one choice fewer.
**σε also means "at / on" for time**: *στις οχτώ* (at eight o'clock), *στις τρεις Μαΐου* (on the third of May). One word, three jobs.

**Position words split into two groups, and you have to learn them as they are.** With **σε**: δίπλα σε (next to), κοντά σε (near), ανάμεσα σε (between), πάνω σε (on top of). With **από**: πίσω από (behind), μπροστά από (in front of), απέναντι από (opposite), κάτω από (under), μακριά από (far from). There's no logic behind it.

**Με τα πόδια** literally "with the feet" means "on foot". Likewise **με το λεωφορείο** (by bus), **με το μετρό** (by metro), **με το αυτοκίνητο** (by car) — all use με + article, where English uses "by".
**Πάρα πολύ** (*PAH-rah poh-LEE*) = "very much indeed", one notch above πολύ. *Ευχαριστώ πάρα πολύ* is the warmest thank-you you can give without sounding over the top.

**Καλή τύχη** = good luck. It belongs to the big family of wishes starting with Καλ-: **Καλή όρεξη** (enjoy your meal), **Καλό ταξίδι** (have a good trip), **Καλή εβδομάδα** (have a good week), **Καλό μήνα** (happy new month — said on the first of every month), **Καλή συνέχεια** (enjoy the rest of your day). Greeks have a wish for almost every beginning.
⚠️ **Πηγαίνετε ευθεία is an imperative**, which will be unpacked in Unit 12. For now, take it as a chunk; you'll hear it in every set of directions.

grammars.title: σε + article = six forms that must become automatic
body: This table deserves a spot on your wall. These six forms appear in almost every everyday Greek sentence.

head: ΣΕ +
Becomes
Say it
Example
rows: στους φίλους μου — to my friends

after: ⚠️ **στη or στην?** Use **στην** when the next word begins with a vowel or κ, π, τ, μπ, ντ, γκ, ξ, ψ: στην Αθήνα, στην πλατεία. Use **στη** before other letters: στη γωνία, στη θάλασσα. When in doubt, write **στην** — it's never considered wrong.
The preposition **από** fuses too, but rarely: από τον → **απ' τον** in fast speech. You can ignore it until you hear it yourself.

grammars.title: Describing position
body: The σε group and the από group. Learning them in pairs is faster than one by one.
after: Directions: **δεξιά** (*dheh-ksee-AH*) right · **αριστερά** (*ah-ree-steh-RAH*) left · **ευθεία** (*ehf-THEE-ah*) straight ahead · **εδώ / εκεί** here / there · **πάνω / κάτω** up / down.

blocks.title: Ready-made phrases for when you're lost
items: **Συγγνώμη, πού είναι …;** — Excuse me, where is …?
**Πώς πάω στο κέντρο;** — How do I get to the center?
**Είναι μακριά;** — Is it far? · **Είναι κοντά;** — Is it near?
**Πόσο μακριά είναι;** — How far is it? The answer usually comes in minutes, not meters: *δέκα λεπτά με τα πόδια*.
**Χάθηκα.** (*KHAH-thee-kah*) — I'm lost. One word that brings help immediately.
⚠️ **Πιο αργά, παρακαλώ.** — More slowly, please. Directions are when you'll need this most: Greeks answer quickly and with lots of hand gestures.

exercises.prompt: Fuse σε with the article. Example: σε + το σπίτι → στο σπίτι.
